card.name: Punctuation before a quantity or share
card.fires_on: Commas, periods and nearby words right after a group description, where a count, percentage or quantifier comes next. Seen in 'Of the patients who...' clauses and in review text before a vague amount.

modes.label: Comma before a percentage
modes.description: A comma closes an 'Of the N patients...' clause, and a percentage of that group follows.
modes.example: Of over 5700 patients enrolled in the risedronate Phase 3 osteoporosis studies<<,>> 21% used H 2

modes.label: Punctuation in book review
modes.description: A period or comma ends a clause about sources, and a quantifier like 'many' or 'some' may follow.
modes.example: Often Weiner does not give an adequate source<<.>> Sometimes whole paragraphs go by without any attribution

modes.label: Word before a count of cases
modes.description: A word in a case-count sentence is followed by a number or share of cases.
